Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Sunosaki Shrine'''|洲崎神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Awa Province|ceb|Awa (baranggay)|ckb|پارێزگای ئاوا (چیبا)|cs|Provincie Awa (Čiba)|de|Provinz Awa (Chiba)|es|Provincia de Awa (Chiba)|fa|ولایت آوا (چیبا)|fr|Province d'Awa (Chiba)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Chiba|hak|Awa-koet (Tōkaidō)|id|Provinsi Awa (Chiba)|it|Awa (provincia, Chiba)|ja|安房国|ko|아와국 (도카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Čiba)|nl|Awa (provincie in Chiba)|pt|Província de Awa (Chiba)|ru|Ава (Канто)|simple|Awa Province (Chiba)|sk|Awa (provincia, Čiba)|sr|Провинција Ава (Хоншу)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Chiba)|uk|Провінція Ава (Канто)|zh|安房國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Tôkaidô)|zh_yue|安房國|qid=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province}}.

The shrine is enshrined on the mid-slope of Mount Mitarai.

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is as follows:
* '''{{ill|Ame no Hiratome|ja|天比理刀咩命|qid=Q85879124|lt=Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto}}''' (あまのひりのめのみこと){{refnest|group="Notes"|The name and reading of the deity follow the “Sanpai no Shiori” distributed by Susaki Shrine.}}
*: She is the consort of {{ill|Awa Shrine|abstract|Q705547|fr|Awa-jinja|ja|安房神社|zh|安房神社|qid=Q705547}}’s enshrined deity {{ill|Futodama|it|Futodama|ja|フトダマ|ru|Футодама|simple|Futodama|zh|布刀玉命|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ama-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, and was originally called “Susa no Kami.”

== Variations in the deity’s name ==
The notation of the deity’s name differs in historical sources as follows:
* Amahiri'''no'''me-no-Mikoto  
*: According to the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}. Works such as {{ill|Suzuka Tsuratane|ja|鈴鹿連胤|qid=Q6536446}}’s {{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|ja|神社覈録|qid=Q11590708}}, the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|ja|教部省|ru|Министерство религий Японии|uk|Міністерство релігій Японії|qid=Q4294653}}-compiled {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}, and the “Sanpai no Shiori” distributed by Susaki Shrine follow this notation.
* Amahiri'''to'''me-no-Mikoto (あめのひりとめのみこと)  
*: According to sources older than the Jinmyōchō, such as the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301}}, {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}, and {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}. Documents such as “Susaki Daimyōjin Yui-sho Kyūki” and “Sunomiya Shrine Records” record the deity under this name.
It has been suggested that this discrepancy arose because the Jinmyōchō mistakenly wrote the character “乃” instead of “刀” for the name originally recorded as Amahiritome-no-Mikoto in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|cs|Rikkokuši|de|Rikkokushi|es|Rikkokushi|eu|Rikkokushi|fa|شش تاریخ ملی|fr|Rikkokushi|it|Rikkokushi|ja|六国史|ko|육국사|pt|Rikkokushi|ru|Риккокуси|simple|Rikkokushi|zh|六國史|qid=Q1151168|lt=official histories}}<ref name="kamigami">Kenichi Tanigawa (ed.), *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Sites – Vol. 11 Kantō* (Hakusuisha, December 1984)</ref>.

According to the “Kanemaru Family Genealogical Record” ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 2 [{{ill|1597|ab|1597|af|1597|als|1597|am|1597 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1597|ar|1597|ary|1597|arz|1597|ast|1597|avk|1597|az|1597|azb|۱۵۹۷ (میلادی)|ban|1597|bar|1597|bcl|1597|be|1597|be_x_old|1597|bg|1597|bn|১৫৯৭|bpy|মারি ১৫৯৭|br|1597|bs|1597.|ca|1597|cdo|1597 nièng|ceb|1597|ckb|١٥٩٧|crh|1597|cs|1597|cv|1597|cy|1597|da|1597|de|1597|diq|1597|el|1597|eml|1597|eo|1597|es|1597|et|1597|eu|1597|fa|۱۵۹۷ (میلادی)|fi|1597|fo|1597|fr|1597|frr|1597|fur|1597|fy|1597|ga|1597|gan|1597年|gcr|1597|gd|1597|gl|1597|glk|۱۵۹۷|gv|1597|he|1597|hi|१५९७|hr|1597.|ht|1597 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1597|hy|1597|hyw|1597 թուական|ia|1597|id|1597|ilo|1597|io|1597|is|1597|it|1597|ja|1597年|jv|1597|ka|1597|kaa|1597|kk|1597 жыл|ko|1597년|krc|1597 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1597|la|1597|lb|1597|lij|1597|lmo|1597|lt|1597 m.|lv|1597. gads|mai|१५९७|map_bms|1597|mdf|1597|mg|1597|mhr|1597|mi|1597|mk|1597|mr|इ.स. १५९७|mrj|1597 и|ms|1597|my|၁၅၉၇|mzn|۱۵۹۷|nap|1597|nds|1597|nds_nl|1597|new|सन् १५९७|nl|1597|nn|1597|no|1597|nrm|1597|nso|1597|oc|1597|olo|1597|or|୧୫୯୭|os|1597-æм аз|pa|1597|pl|1597|pnb|1597|pt|1597|qu|1597|ro|1597|ru|1597 год|rue|1597|sa|१५९७|sah|1597|scn|1597|sd|1597ع|se|1597|sh|1597.|shn|1597|simple|1597|sk|1597|sl|1597|smn|1597|sq|1597|sr|1597|su|1597|sv|1597|sw|1597|ta|1597|te|1597|tg|Соли 1597|th|พ.ศ. 2140|tk|1597|tl|1597|tly|1597|tr|1597|tt|1597 ел|uk|1597|ur|1597ء|uz|1597|vec|1597|vi|1597|vls|1597|wa|1597|war|1597|wuu|1597年|xmf|1597|yi|1597|zh|1597年|zh_min_nan|1597 nî|zh_yue|1597年|qid=Q6790}}]), the Sunomiya Kō Shrine in Sunomiya Village, Awa District, later called Sunomiya Myōjin, was regarded as the inner sanctuary and the second shrine, while Susaki Myōjin on Mount Mitarai in Susaki Village was regarded as the worship hall and the first shrine. Based on this, it has been proposed that Susaki Shrine and {{ill|Sunomiya Shrine|ja|洲宮神社|qid=Q11556507}} formed a paired shrine complex enshrining the “Susa no Kami,” with Susaki Shrine as the first shrine and Sunomiya Shrine as the second<ref name="kiso">Medieval Provincial Ichinomiya System Research Group (ed.), *Fundamental Research on the Medieval Provincial Ichinomiya System* (Iwata Shoin, February 2000)</ref><ref name="kamigami" />.

Shrine tradition also recounts that in Yōrō 1 ({{ill|717|ab|717|af|717|am|717 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|717|ar|717|ary|717|ast|717|avk|717|az|717|azb|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|be|717|be_x_old|717|bg|717|bn|৭১৭|bpy|মারি ৭১৭|br|717|bs|717.|ca|717|cdo|717 nièng|ceb|717|ckb|٧١٧|crh|717|cs|717|cv|717|cy|717|da|717|de|717|el|717|eml|717|eo|717|es|717|et|717|eu|717|fa|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|fi|717|fo|717|fr|717|fy|717|ga|717|gan|717年|gd|717|gl|717|hak|717-ngièn|he|717|hi|717|hr|717.|ht|717 (almanak jilyen)|hu|717|hy|717|id|717|ilo|717|io|717|is|717|it|717|ja|717年|jv|717|ka|717|kaa|717|kk|717 жыл|ko|717년|la|717|lb|717|lij|717|lmo|717|lt|717 m.|lv|717. gads|map_bms|717|mdf|717|mg|717|mhr|717|mk|717|mr|इ.स. ७१७|mrj|717 и|ms|717|mzn|۷۱۷|nah|717|nap|717|nds|717|new|सन् ७१७|nl|717|nn|717|no|717|nrm|717|nso|717|oc|717|or|୭୧୭|os|717-æм аз|pl|717|pnb|717|pt|717|qu|717|ro|717|ru|717 год|rue|717|sa|७१७|scn|717|sd|717ع|sh|717.|shn|717|si|717|sk|717|sl|717|smn|717|sq|717|sr|717|su|717|sv|717|sw|717|tg|Соли 717|th|พ.ศ. 1260|tk|717|tl|717|tly|717|tr|717|tt|717 ел|uk|717|ur|717ء|uz|717|vec|717|vi|717|vls|717|war|717|wuu|717年|xmf|717|zh|717年|zh_min_nan|717 nî|zh_yue|717年|qid=Q23532}}), a great earthquake buried Kanegae Pond within the precincts, and a great serpent guarding a subterranean bell caused calamities. {{ill|En no Gyōja|de|En no Gyōja|es|En no Gyōja|fa|ان نو گیوجا|fr|En no Gyōja|he|אן נו גיוג'ה|it|En no Gyōja|ja|役小角|ko|엔노 오즈누|pl|En-no Gyōja|ru|Эн-но Гёдзя|sh|En no Gyōja|uk|Ен-но-Ґьодзя|zh|役小角|qid=Q198946}} is said to have performed prayers for seven days and nights, received a divine oracle, and subdued the serpent, thereby removing the disaster. It is also said that En no Gyōja placed sacred stones for maritime safety on the shore in front of the beach torii and at Awaguchi Shrine in {{ill|Yokosuka|af|Yokosuka|ar|يوكوسوكا (كاناغاوا)|arz|يوكوسوكا, كاناجاوا|azb|یوکوسوکا، کاناقاوا|ban|Yokosuka, Kanagawa|be|Якосука|bg|Йокосука|ca|Yokosuka|ce|Йокосука|ceb|Yokosuka|cs|Jokosuka|de|Yokosuka|el|Γιοκοσούκα|eo|Jokosuko|es|Yokosuka (Kanagawa)|et|Yokosuka|eu|Yokosuka|fa|یوکوسوکا، کاناگاوا|fi|Yokosuka|fr|Yokosuka|ga|Yokosuka|gl|Yokosuka|he|יוקוסוקה|hu|Jokoszuka (Kanagava)|hy|Յոկոսուկա|id|Yokosuka|it|Yokosuka|ja|横須賀市|ka|იოკოსუკა|ko|요코스카시|lt|Jokosuka|mg|Yokosuka|ms|Yokosuka, Kanagawa|mzn|یوکوسوکا، کاناگاوا|nl|Yokosuka|nn|Yokosuka|no|Yokosuka|pl|Yokosuka|pt|Yokosuka|ro|Yokosuka|ru|Йокосука|sh|Jokosuka|simple|Yokosuka, Kanagawa|sk|Jokosuka|sr|Јокосука|sv|Yokosuka|szl|Yokosuka|tg|Ёкосука|th|โยโกซูกะ|tl|Yokosuka|tr|Yokosuka|tt|Йокосука|tum|Yokosuka|uk|Йокосука|ur|یوکوسکا، کناگوا|uz|Yokosuka|vi|Yokosuka|war|Yokosuka, Kanagawa|wuu|横须贺市|zh|橫須賀市|zh_classical|橫須賀市|zh_min_nan|Yokosuka-chhī|zh_yue|橫須賀|qid=Q200578|lt=Yokosuka}}{{refnest|group="Notes"|The paired sacred stone is enshrined as the sacred object of Awaguchi Shrine in Yoshii, Yokosuka City.}}. == Overview ==
=== Medieval period ===
“Awa Province Amahiritome-no-Kami” appears frequently in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|cs|Rikkokuši|de|Rikkokushi|es|Rikkokushi|eu|Rikkokushi|fa|شش تاریخ ملی|fr|Rikkokushi|it|Rikkokushi|ja|六国史|ko|육국사|pt|Rikkokushi|ru|Риккокуси|simple|Rikkokushi|zh|六國史|qid=Q1151168}} and received successive promotions in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|fa|شینکای (رتبه الهی)|ja|神階|qid=Q11591025}} (see {{ill|Susaki Shrine|ja|洲崎神社|simple|Susaki Shrine|qid=Q11556513|lt=below}}).

In the {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) edition of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, it is recorded as “Kōshin Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto Shrine, Major, original name Susa-no-Kami” in Awa District, Awa Province, and was ranked as a major shrine. Susaki Shrine is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} of this shrine, the other being Sunomiya Shrine, and disputes over which was the true Shikinaisha continued from the Edo period.

From ancient times, the shrine collected tolls from passing vessels, indicating control over maritime passage rights and sea checkpoints. This suggests that in the early and mid-medieval periods, Susaki Shrine held the greatest authority and power in Awa Province<ref>Tsuneari Takigawa, “The Satomi Clan of Bōsō and Maritime Transport in Edo Bay,” *Chiba Shigaku* No. 24, 1994</ref>.

though large-scale repairs occurred after the mid-Edo period. It is designated a Tangible Cultural Property of Tateyama City.

The Zuijin Gate was built during the {{ill|Hōei|fa|هوئی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hōei|ja|宝永|ko|호에이|ru|Хоэй|simple|Hōei|sr|Хоеи|sv|Hōei|tr|Hōei|zh|寶永|qid=Q1145262}} era, and 150 steps lead from behind it to the shrine buildings.

Outside the beach torii stands a rounded stone called the “Sacred Stone,” said to be one of a pair dedicated from the Dragon Palace, the other enshrined at {{ill|Awaguchi Shrine|ja|安房口神社|qid=Q59282598}} on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|az|Miura yarımadası|ceb|Miura Hantō|de|Miura-Halbinsel|es|Península de Miura|fa|شبه‌جزیره میئورا|fr|Péninsule de Miura|id|Semenanjung Miura|it|Penisola di Miura|ja|三浦半島|ko|미우라반도|nl|Miura (schiereiland)|pl|Miura (półwysep)|pt|Península de Miura|ru|Миура (полуостров)|sv|Miurahalvön|th|คาบสมุทรมิอูระ|tr|Miura Yarımadası|vi|Bán đảo Miura|zh|三浦半島|qid=Q536757}}. The Awaguchi stone represents “A-gyō,” while the Susaki stone represents “Un-gyō,” together guarding the entrance to Tokyo Bay{{refnest|group="Notes"|Information board.}}.

Because the sea before the shrine is a key maritime route into Tokyo Bay, many votive plaques dedicated by ship captains for safe voyages were once seen before the war.

After the shrine suffered major damage from the {{ill|Typhoon Faxai|ja|令和元年房総半島台風|ko|태풍 파사이 (2019년)|uk|Факсай (тайфун)|vi|Bão Faxai (2019)|zh|颱風法茜 (2019年)|zh_min_nan|Hong-thai Faxai (2019 nî)|qid=Q67170176}} in {{ill|Reiwa era|ar|فترة رييوا|az|Reyva erası|ban|Reiwa|be|Рэйва|bo|རེ་བ|bug|ᨑᨙᨕᨗᨓ|ca|Període Reiwa|cdo|Lêng-huò|cs|Období Reiwa|de|Reiwa-Zeit|eo|Reiva-epoko|es|Era Reiwa|fa|دوره ریوا|fi|Reiwa-kausi|fr|Ère Reiwa|haw|Reiwa Makahiki|he|תקופת ראיווה|hi|रेइवा युग|hu|Reiva-kor|id|Zaman Reiwa|it|Periodo Reiwa|ja|令和|jv|Reiwa|ka|რეივა|ko|레이와 시대|lt|Reiva laikotarpis|mn|Рэйва|ms|Zaman Reiwa|nl|Reiwa|no|Reiwa|oc|Reiwa|pl|Reiwa|pt|Período Reiwa|ro|Perioada Reiwa|ru|Рэйва|simple|Reiwa era|sk|Obdobie Reiwa|sl|Obdobje Reiva|sq|Periudha Reiva|sv|Reiwa|th|ยุคเรวะ|tr|Reiwa Dönemi|uk|Період Рейва|uz|Reiva|vi|Thời kỳ Lệnh Hòa|wuu|令和|zh|令和|zh_classical|令和|zh_min_nan|Lēng-hô|zh_yue|令和|qid=Q62609017}}, donations were received from various supporters, including the Tokyo talent agency {{ill|Johnny & Associates|ca|Johnny & Associates|de|Smile-Up|es|Johnny & Associates|fa|شرکت جانی و همکاران|fr|Johnny & Associates|hu|Johnny & Associates|id|Johnny & Associates|it|Johnny & Associates|ja|ジャニーズ事務所|ko|자니스 사무소|pl|Johnny & Associates|pt|Johnny & Associates|ru|Johnny & Associates|simple|Johnny & Associates|sv|Johnny & Associates|th|จอห์นนีแอนด์อะโซชีเอท|tr|Johnny & Associates|uk|Johnny & Associates|ur|جونی اینڈ ایسوسی ایٹس|vi|Johnny & Associates|wuu|杰尼斯公司|zh|SMILE-UP.|qid=Q11728013|lt=Johnny & Associates (then; now SMILE-UP.)}}, and used for reconstruction such as rebuilding torii of the Inari sub-shrine. A commemorative stone expressing gratitude for this support stands within the precincts.

== Festivals ==
